NA Electrical Design Training Day 2_Part B

说话人1: 00:00:00 - 00:00:24

Next, I will briefly introduce lighting design, focusing on the differences. The content includes lighting-related standards and regulations, energy-saving issues, and lighting control systems, which are relatively straightforward.

说话人1: 00:00:25 - 00:00:35

Lighting design primarily involves lighting control systems. The emergency lighting portion has already been discussed and requires no further elaboration. Illuminance calculation is a well-known aspect.

说话人1: 00:00:36 - 00:01:42

For lighting illuminance requirements, we previously mentioned that emergency lighting must achieve at least 10 lux. Other illuminance standards primarily refer to the recommended guidelines in the Illuminating Engineering Society (IES) Handbook.

For lighting illuminance requirements, we previously mentioned that emergency lighting must achieve at least 10 lux. Other illuminance standards primarily refer to the recommended guidelines in the Illuminating Engineering Society (IES) Handbook.

Streetlight design must comply with each city’s specific regulations. Additionally, ASHRAE 90.1, as an energy efficiency standard, has been incorporated into building codes, imposing clear limits on lighting power consumption for different functional spaces.

Currently, in Canada and the United States, these energy efficiency requirements have become mandatory regulations. This new rule may not yet be implemented domestically, so we will not elaborate further here.

说话人1: 00:01:43 - 00:02:59

It is well known that certain luminaires must comply with the ASHRAE 90.1 standard, which has been incorporated into building codes in the United States and Canada. To meet these requirements, LED luminaires are typically used exclusively.

It is well known that certain luminaires must comply with the ASHRAE 90.1 standard, which has been incorporated into building codes in the United States and Canada. To meet these requirements, LED luminaires are typically used exclusively.

Additionally, lighting control systems encompass various approaches:
- One method utilizes occupancy sensors to maintain illumination when activity is detected and delays turning off lights when unoccupied.
- Another employs a central lighting control system, such as scheduling lights to turn on at 7:30 AM and off at 5:30 PM on workdays (emergency lighting excluded).

Notably, central lighting control systems are often integrated with environmental comfort control systems. For specialized building projects like theaters, stadiums, and museums, lighting design requires tailored considerations.

In North America, electrical engineers conduct lighting design work based on these principles.

说话人1: 00:02:59 - 00:04:08

In North America, electrical engineers conduct lighting design work based on these principles.

说话人1: 00:02:59 - 00:04:08

Sometimes it’s necessary to collaborate with architects, interior designers, or landscape architects for non-functional lighting designs such as landscape lighting or architectural lighting. This part is handled by them, while we provide power supply support.

As for regular functional lighting, it’s usually designed by us. For scenarios with higher requirements for specialized lighting, such as theater lighting, professional lighting consultants are typically hired for the design, and we take care of the power supply.

This is an overview of the entire design process.

说话人1: 00:04:08 - 00:04:15

Regarding how to proceed with the design, these are rather basic points, so I won’t elaborate further.

说话人1: 00:04:15 - 00:05:25

说话人1: 00:04:08 - 00:04:15

Regarding how to proceed with the design, these are rather basic points, so I won’t elaborate further.

说话人1: 00:04:15 - 00:05:25

From an energy-saving perspective, lighting control is crucial. In certain scenarios, lighting control can be integrated with HVAC systems to achieve energy efficiency, such as using occupancy sensor switches to simultaneously control room lighting and air conditioning systems. In North America, it was once common practice to use nightlights that were directly controlled by breakers in the distribution panel, but current energy efficiency standards conflict with ASHRAE 90.1, leading to adjustments in relevant regulations.

Beyond basic on/off controls, energy-efficient lighting control also includes dimmer switches for adjustable lighting. For outdoor lighting, photo sensors are employed for light-sensitive control, automatically activating lighting equipment when ambient illumination is insufficient and turning it off at dawn.

说话人1: 00:05:25 - 00:06:01

The central control system has become quite advanced, with some luminaires now supporting dimming control via smartphones. This type of functionality is relatively easy to implement, and various new products have emerged in the market, especially in China where the options are more abundant. These technologies primarily focus on enhancing entertainment value and energy efficiency, rather than being directly related to life safety. The discussion here mainly revolves around lighting design.

说话人1: 00:06:01 - 00:06:57

说话人1: 00:06:01 - 00:06:57

The documents we need to submit include lighting calculations. Although AGI32 files are more commonly used for such calculations, under normal circumstances, we do not perform illuminance calculations for lighting design drawings unless specifically required, in order to save time. As long as the estimated results roughly meet the standards, it is acceptable.

Regarding lighting design, the ASHRAE 90.1 standard requires the completion of relevant paperwork. Specifically, the lighting design scheme must be confirmed based on the standard requirements, taking into account the number of luminaires and the power consumption of individual lights. The lighting layout must ensure compliance with all requirements of ASHRAE 90.1. Additionally, the lighting schedule is also one of the mandatory documents.

说话人1: 00:06:57 - 00:07:21

说话人1: 00:06:57 - 00:07:21

After the project is completed, it is necessary to verify the illuminance. Typically, a lux meter is used to directly measure the illuminance values in various areas to confirm whether they meet the design requirements. This is a crucial step in the lighting design phase.

说话人1: 00:07:21 - 00:07:53

During the construction phase, the lighting system is typically handled by electrical contractors, who are required to submit construction drawings.

In the commissioning phase, especially when involving lighting control systems, a series of tasks must be completed, such as:
- Illuminance testing
- Sensor operability testing
- Dimmer testing
- Overall functional verification of the central lighting control system

As-built drawings and operation and maintenance manuals are also essential.

说话人1: 00:08:04 - 00:10:01

Due to time constraints and multiple agenda items still to be discussed, I’ll briefly cover the cable installation section.

Cable conductors are primarily categorized into three types: copper-core, aluminum-core, and fiber optic. Selection depends on voltage levels and intended applications, such as communication, signal transmission, or power distribution. Fire resistance is another critical consideration for cables.

In North America, cable installation requires selecting appropriate fire-rated cables based on building types. Building codes classify structures as combustible or noncombustible, with clear specifications on cable types for each category.

In North America, cable installation requires selecting appropriate fire-rated cables based on building types. Building codes classify structures as combustible or noncombustible, with clear specifications on cable types for each category.

Fire-resistant cables are primarily used for life safety systems or power supply, while flame-retardant cables are suitable for general purposes. Flame-retardant cables also have different grades, which must be selected according to building types.

Cables can be installed in various ways, including open wiring and cable tray systems. Additionally, there are special-purpose cables for specific applications.

说话人1: 00:10:01 - 00:10:49

Cables can be installed in various ways, including open wiring and cable tray systems. Additionally, there are special-purpose cables for specific applications.

说话人1: 00:10:01 - 00:10:49

For example, VFD cables may generate noise if special cables are not used. In situations with high fire safety requirements, metal-based fire-resistant cables, namely MI (Mineral Insulated) cables, must be employed. Grounding and equipotential bonding use surface-insulated conductors or bare wires, with specific applications adhering to the Electrical Code and Building Code. High-voltage transmission lines typically utilize HV/MV Aluminum Stranded with Steel Core. Below are relevant example images.

说话人1: 00:10:50 - 00:11:32

Seller Station or power plants use medium-high voltage cables. On the left is the VFD, likely a domestic enclosed busway product; the right side is called Cable Bus, which differs from enclosed busways.

说话人1: 00:10:50 - 00:11:32

Seller Station or power plants use medium-high voltage cables. On the left is the VFD, likely a domestic enclosed busway product; the right side is called Cable Bus, which differs from enclosed busways.

This diagram selection is incorrect. Cable Bus is actually a structure formed by integrating multiple cables, whereas enclosed busways encapsulate the Bus (busbars). The application scenarios of both have been explained here.

说话人1: 00:11:33 - 00:11:49

There are certain differences between ordinary wires and cables. Cables not only have an insulation layer but also include a protective layer, and some cables even have shielding functionality.

说话人1: 00:11:50 - 00:12:40

Wires can be divided into two types: single-core and stranded. Typically, wires of size 8 AWG and above adopt a stranded structure, while wires of size 12 AWG and below use a single-core structure.

说话人1: 00:11:50 - 00:12:40

Wires can be divided into two types: single-core and stranded. Typically, wires of size 8 AWG and above adopt a stranded structure, while wires of size 12 AWG and below use a single-core structure.

Connections between wires must meet specific requirements, which are all basic standards in construction. Additionally, under different environmental conditions, such as waterproof or explosion-proof requirements, corresponding considerations are also necessary.

The selection criteria for cable and wire sizes will be explained in detail in subsequent slides. This is a basic introduction to wire conduit installation.

说话人1: 00:12:41 - 00:13:27

In North America, conduit pipes are primarily categorized into several types. One is EMT (Electrical Metallic Tubing), a relatively lightweight piping material; another is Rigid Metallic Tubing Conduit.

说话人1: 00:12:41 - 00:13:27

In North America, conduit pipes are primarily categorized into several types. One is EMT (Electrical Metallic Tubing), a relatively lightweight piping material; another is Rigid Metallic Tubing Conduit.

EMT pipes are widely used indoors, while outdoors, particularly for underground sections, reinforced PVC pipes are typically employed. For structures like brick or concrete walls, reinforced steel pipes or metallic conduits are more commonly used.

Rigid and Non-Rigid pipes differ in their wall protection capabilities, while PVC pipes fall into a separate category.

说话人1: 00:13:28 - 00:14:13

Rigid and Non-Rigid pipes differ in their wall protection capabilities, while PVC pipes fall into a separate category.

说话人1: 00:13:28 - 00:14:13

Typically used in damp environments or underground locations. Flexible Metal Conduit is more commonly employed in suspended ceilings or within decorative wall structures in North America. Some conduits require consideration of window pipe design, interconnection methods, support structures, and outdoor usage requirements. In hazardous-rated areas, explosion-proof measures must also be considered, necessitating special connection fittings. Additionally, cable trays serve as crucial components.

说话人1: 00:14:13 - 00:14:32

Various forms such as ventilated or non-ventilated, with or without covers, mesh-type or ladder-type, all fall within the construction scope. In terms of materials, both metal and fiberglass options are available. In practical applications of cable trays, appropriate types should be selected based on specific requirements.

说话人1: 00:14:33 - 00:14:50

According to electrical code requirements, when cables of different voltage levels are installed in the same cable tray, barriers must be installed for separation. Additionally, both the cable tray itself and the installed cables must be properly grounded.

说话人1: 00:14:50 - 00:15:01

For island-type window ducts, fireproof treatment is mandatory when passing through firewalls. Additionally, equipment such as Wireway or Splitter should also pay attention to such issues.

说话人1: 00:15:02 - 00:15:23

Additionally, they are also referred to as Gutter, primarily used for small-scale projects. In the Control Panel, Panduit is typically employed to secure cables, making it suitable for applications in extreme environments. Panduit’s installation methods include indoor installation.

说话人1: 00:15:23 - 00:15:46

说话人1: 00:15:23 - 00:15:46

Free Air refers to the direct installation of cables in the air, though they can also be installed in cable trays. Additionally, installations may occur in base-level equipment rooms or under floors (such as beneath Flow systems).

Raceway primarily denotes pipeline systems like Conduit or Wireway, which are typically installed indoors. Outdoor installations employ other laying methods.

说话人1: 00:15:47 - 00:16:23

You can choose to install wires in the air using the overhead line method. Additionally, you may opt for conduit wiring, cable trench installation, direct burial, or the Duct Bank method.

Duct Bank refers to encasing conduits containing wires in concrete for fixation, typically suitable for environments requiring high compressive strength, especially in hazardous areas where explosion-proof treatment is necessary.

说话人1: 00:16:24 - 00:16:53

In damp or wet environments, weatherproof measures should be adopted.

说话人1: 00:16:24 - 00:16:53

In damp or wet environments, weatherproof measures should be adopted.

PVC materials are widely used due to their anti-corrosion properties, whereas ordinary metal materials are prone to corrosion. Cathodic Protection is a protective method, but it will not be discussed in detail here.

说话人1: 00:16:53 - 00:17:53

In domestic regulations, the relevant requirements for cables and wires passing through conduits are clearly specified.

First, attention must be paid to the installation spacing of cables and wires in conduits. It is particularly important to note that cables are not allowed to be spliced in the middle. Therefore, when the cable length is long, the number of 90-degree bends in the installation route must not exceed 3 to 4, otherwise it will affect the installation process.

In addition, the installation of cable trays must avoid conflicts with pipelines or ducts from other disciplines. Regarding the number of wires allowed in a conduit, the regulations provide detailed reference tables.

Building codes have specific provisions for such installation requirements.

说话人1: 00:17:53 - 00:18:50

Buildings are classified into combustible and non-combustible categories, and the grade of flame-retardant cables must be selected based on the specific environment. For example, above ceilings or in certain areas, specific types of flame-retardant cables must be used, and these details are clearly stipulated in building codes.

Electrical codes cover aspects such as the sizing calculations for conductors and cables, conductor installation in conduits, cable trays, and laying requirements.

说话人1: 00:18:51 - 00:20:00

Electrical codes cover aspects such as the sizing calculations for conductors and cables, conductor installation in conduits, cable trays, and laying requirements.

说话人1: 00:18:51 - 00:20:00

The selection of cables and wires has special requirements regarding radiation. Typically, manufacturers provide recommended solutions, which have been confirmed to comply with electrical codes and building regulations.

For communication systems and security systems, although the requirements differ from those of fire protection systems, there are also specific standards. For example, communication systems have special requirements for the installation of cables and wires, as well as cable trays and raceways, which are detailed in the TIA/EIA standards.

In addition, the installation of cable trays and bus ducts must comply with NEMA or manufacturer standards. These standards are not commonly encountered in practical applications. Furthermore, local power authorities may also have relevant requirements.

In addition, the installation of cable trays and bus ducts must comply with NEMA or manufacturer standards. These standards are not commonly encountered in practical applications. Furthermore, local power authorities may also have relevant requirements.

说话人1: 00:20:00 - 00:20:31

It may also have some special requirements, such as the relevant regulations imposed by local power and telecommunications companies on communication facilities. Next, I will briefly introduce the installation of conductor cables, cable trays, and conduit pipes. This section is relatively straightforward and does not involve too many complex technical details.

说话人1: 00:20:31 - 00:20:35

How to calculate the cross-sectional area of wires or cables? There are two main codes and standards involved: NEC CEC is a mandatory code, while the HWE standard is non-mandatory. I mention the latter because of its importance.

说话人1: 00:20:36 - 00:21:11

说话人1: 00:20:36 - 00:21:11

Since the cable and conductor calculation and selection methods mentioned in CEC and NEC are applicable to special cases and are rarely used in daily work, special attention should be paid when selecting cable types.

说话人1: 00:21:11 - 00:22:05

When selecting cables and wires, two factors must be considered: type and cross-sectional area. The type should be determined based on its function and usage environment, while the cross-sectional area needs to be calculated according to the current-carrying capacity. The key indicator of current-carrying capacity is the magnitude of the load current, which serves as the basis for selection.

The load type is also crucial, including different scenarios such as general loads, motor loads, or complete equipment. Additionally, it is necessary to consider whether the load is single-phase, three-phase, or two-phase, as well as the installation environment, such as whether it is buried underground.

说话人1: 00:22:05 - 00:25:13

说话人1: 00:22:05 - 00:25:13

During the installation of cables or conductors, situations may arise where a single circuit employs multiple installation methods simultaneously, such as underground, overhead, and indoor. In such cases, we must consider the most stringent conditions (i.e., the worst case). The NEC and CEC standards provide detailed tables covering current-carrying capacity data for various installation methods, including:

Conductor Material: Copper or aluminum (both are used in North America, though aluminum has lower conductivity and requires a larger cross-section for the same current capacity).

Installation Methods:

Overhead installation (single-phase or three-phase)

Conduit installation

Direct burial

Raceway installation (e.g., bus ducts or concrete-encased conduits)

Installation Methods:

Overhead installation (single-phase or three-phase)

Conduit installation

Direct burial

Raceway installation (e.g., bus ducts or concrete-encased conduits)

Additionally, the ambient temperature correction factor must be considered. For cables installed in trays, adjustments are required based on the number of cables. The baseline value typically refers to the current-carrying capacity of a single cable at 30°C ambient temperature.

Another critical factor is voltage drop. Even if the current-carrying capacity meets requirements, long-distance power transmission may result in a voltage drop exceeding 5% at the load end, necessitating an increase in conductor cross-section. These factors also apply to conductor selection for the primary and secondary sides of dry-type transformers.

All conditions must be comprehensively evaluated, with the most restrictive scenario serving as the design basis to determine conductor specifications.

说话人1: 00:25:13 - 00:28:30

All conditions must be comprehensively evaluated, with the most restrictive scenario serving as the design basis to determine conductor specifications.

说话人1: 00:25:13 - 00:28:30

We select conductors based on the composite current. Typically, the ampacity of the conductor should be 1.25 times the composite current to ensure compliance with regulations. The same principle applies to the selection of dry-type transformers and individual motors.

Note that although motor protection devices require 6 times the current, the cross-sectional area selection of power supply cables or conductors is still based on 1.25 times the composite current. Special cases involving motors will be discussed in detail in subsequent lessons. This lesson focuses on the method for selecting conductor or cable cross-sections, while the next lecture will cover the selection of circuit breakers or fuses.

For a single motor, conductor selection is calculated at 1.25 times the composite current. The approach differs for multiple motors: the selection of main feeders is not based on multiplying each motor’s composite current by 125%, but rather on taking 125% of the largest motor’s current plus the sum of the normal currents of all other motors. This refers to the sizing of the uppermost main feeder, not branch circuits.

For packaged equipment (such as air conditioning units or other industrial packaged equipment, referred to as “Skeed”), the selection method follows manufacturer-provided parameters. Manufacturers typically provide two key parameters: MCA (Minimum Current Ampacity) and MCP (Maximum Over Current Protection). MCA is used to determine conductor cross-sections, while MOP is used to select circuit protection devices (fuses or circuit breakers). In this case, the manufacturer’s specified values can be used directly without additional calculation factors.

[Note: The term “消货梦” in the original text appears to be a technical term, but its accurate equivalent could not be determined from context, so it is retained as-is; “融钻器” was corrected to “熔断器” (fuse) as it was clearly a typographical error.]

说话人1: 00:28:30 - 00:30:00

When the conductor is long and passes through different environments, it is essential to consider the most severe conditions, such as underground, outdoor, and especially rooftop environments. In summer, severe western sun exposure causes extremely high surface temperatures on the conductor, which significantly affects its current-carrying capacity. Therefore, the design should be based on the most severe conditions.

Multiple coefficients need to be considered, such as the temperature coefficient and multi-conductor parallel coefficient, which can be found in relevant tables. After calculating all coefficients, compare the conductor’s actual current-carrying capacity with the required amperage.

Additionally, the voltage drop issue must be addressed. If no other improvement measures are available, the voltage drop can be reduced by the following methods: adjusting transformer tap settings, performing reactive power compensation, increasing the conductor cross-sectional area, or raising the voltage level. Among these, increasing the conductor cross-sectional area is the most commonly used method.

The design must be based on the maximum current and the most severe environmental conditions. The relevant calculation formulas are as follows.

说话人1: 00:30:00 - 00:30:33

In fact, this principle has already been fully explained. The specific calculation formula is as follows:

First, calculate the base current to determine the required current magnitude; then, for different types of loads, multiply by the corresponding correction factors according to the aforementioned calculation criteria; finally, select the cross-sectional size of the conductor.

The above outlines the specific process for conductor selection.

说话人1: 00:30:35 - 00:32:19

This section will introduce the selection of low-voltage circuit breakers, fuses, and disconnect switches. First, a brief overview of the types of low-voltage circuit breakers: the first is MCCB (Molded Case Circuit Breaker), and the other is low-voltage power circuit breakers, typically installed in switchgear. Their trip mechanisms include magnetic trip, thermal trip, and combined magnetic-thermal trip. Installation methods mainly consist of plug-in, bolt-on, and draw-out.

Regarding protection coordination, it is primarily divided into full rated and series rated, which will be explained in detail later. Generally, circuit breakers below 250A use an 80% rating—for example, a 200A breaker protects at 160A—while frame sizes of 250A or 400A and above allow for 100% protection, meaning a 400A breaker can operate normally at 400A current.

Additionally, circuit breakers can be categorized by application, including standard type, General HVAC (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning), and RGFCI (Residual Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter), among others.

说话人1: 00:32:20 - 00:32:51

On the left is a bolt-on circuit breaker, typically installed inside distribution panels with a wide range of applications. On the right is a low-voltage power circuit breaker, primarily designed for installation in switchgear. The left type is usually mounted in accessory panels, and here we discuss both full-rated and series-rated configurations.

说话人1: 00:32:51 - 00:34:22

说话人1: 00:32:51 - 00:34:22

The discussion here focuses on the interruption of short-circuit currents. Fully Rated means that when a short circuit occurs at this point, neither circuit breaker will trip. On the other hand, Series Rated implies that if the short-circuit current here is 25kA, and the downstream circuit breaker can only interrupt 22kA, the entire burden of interrupting the short-circuit current will fall on the upstream circuit breaker. Although a 65kA circuit breaker is capable of handling this task, it will result in a larger outage area.

In some cases, to save costs or because the load is non-critical (such as residential or non-essential commercial facilities), a larger outage area may be acceptable. This reflects the coordination of circuit breakers and their different operating modes. Clearly, Fully Rated is the superior choice, but for small loads (e.g., where the short-circuit current is only 50kA), using a 65kA circuit breaker, while feasible, requires consideration of the fact that the higher the interrupting capacity of a circuit breaker, the more expensive and physically larger it becomes.

说话人1: 00:34:24 - 00:35:06

This is a photo of an electronic trip unit for a circuit breaker. Electronic trip units are typically used in circuit breakers rated 400A and above, offering multiple functions. For example, they allow adjustment of the circuit breaker’s trip current settings, such as modifying a 400A breaker to operate at 200A or 250A.

Additionally, electronic trip units feature replaceability, making them more convenient to use. In contrast, the trip units in low-capacity circuit breakers lack this flexibility.

说话人1: 00:35:06 - 00:35:51

Circuit breakers offer more powerful functionality compared to the combination of disconnect switches and fuses, and provide greater convenience in protection coordination. Circuit breakers primarily serve the following functions:

First, they can function as switching devices;
Second, they enable overcurrent protection and overload protection;
Additionally, they can protect both motors and general loads (such as lighting equipment), as well as cables or conductors.

These circuit breakers come in various specifications including 1P, 2P, 3P, and 4P. Among them, the 4P model can interrupt the neutral wire, while the 2P model is specifically designed to interrupt two phase wires—a configuration unique to North American designs.

说话人1: 00:35:52 - 00:37:38

说话人1: 00:35:52 - 00:37:38

One of the key specifications of a circuit breaker is its short-circuit breaking capacity, the rating of which depends on voltage and the manufacturer’s technical parameters.

Low-voltage circuit breakers typically feature multiple protection functions, including instantaneous trip, short-time delay, long-time delay, and ground fault protection (the “G” in LSIG stands for ground protection).

Compared to fuses and ordinary switches, circuit breakers offer significant advantages:
- Support remote trip control functionality
- Equipped with auxiliary contacts (such as observer switches)
- High-capacity breakers also include electronic trip modules, enabling automatic tripping during undervoltage conditions or accepting remote control commands
- Additional features like mechanical interlocks

Depending on the application scenario, circuit breakers can be used in switchgear, motor control centers, distribution boards, and other equipment.

说话人1: 00:37:39 - 00:38:35

Depending on the application scenario, circuit breakers can be used in switchgear, motor control centers, distribution boards, and other equipment.

说话人1: 00:37:39 - 00:38:35

This is about the setting principles for circuit breakers.

For feeder protection, the setting value is 125% of the load current. For dry-type transformer protection, the same 125% of the rated current is applied. Protection for non-motor loads also uses 125% of the rated current.

However, protection for motor loads differs, requiring a setting of 250% of the rated current to avoid the motor’s starting current. For variable frequency drive loads, the protection setting remains at 125% of the rated current. As for complete equipment, the setting is based on the MOP value.

The setting value for fire protection equipment, as mentioned earlier, is 600%.

说话人1: 00:38:35 - 00:39:25

This circuit breaker does not have composite protection functionality.

The setting value for fire protection equipment, as mentioned earlier, is 600%.

说话人1: 00:38:35 - 00:39:25

This circuit breaker does not have composite protection functionality.

Regarding ground fault protection, the 600V 1000A and 208V 2000A configurations typically provide four protection functions. Ground fault protection adopts the primary protection method, where long-time delay, short-time delay, and instantaneous protections serve as primary protections. It is generally unnecessary to activate all functions simultaneously.

The tripping device employs an electronic tripping method, applicable to circuit breakers with ratings of 400A and above. The selection methodology for circuit breakers has been previously explained in detail.

说话人1: 00:39:26 - 00:41:06

The tripping device employs an electronic tripping method, applicable to circuit breakers with ratings of 400A and above. The selection methodology for circuit breakers has been previously explained in detail.

说话人1: 00:39:26 - 00:41:06

In addition to selecting circuit breakers based on frame size, it is also necessary to determine their rated interrupting capacity (IC rating) through short-circuit current calculations. The coordination between these parameters requires the use of calculation software, such as power system analysis tools like ETAP or SKM, to plot current-time curves.

Regarding overload protection, circuit breakers can also serve an overload protection function. For motor overload protection, there are specific regulations: motors below half horsepower uniformly use 15-amp protection, while those above half horsepower require additional overload protection devices.

The core difference between circuit breakers and fuses lies in the fact that fuses do not consider current magnitude—they simply interrupt the circuit upon a short-circuit occurrence—whereas circuit breakers must be configured based on specific parameters.

The main distinction between circuit breakers and contactors is that circuit breakers can interrupt both load current and short-circuit current, while contactors are only used for control circuits and can interrupt load current but cannot break short-circuit current. Disconnect switches similarly only have the capability to interrupt load current.

As for fuses, their working principle is…

说话人1: 00:41:07 - 00:41:42

Fuses come in various grades and types, such as time-delay, quick-acting, high-voltage, low-voltage, and AC-type.

Generally, time-delay fuses have relatively lower breaking currents, while quick-acting fuses require higher breaking currents. These are the fundamental characteristics of different fuse types.

说话人1: 00:41:43 - 00:42:09

Generally, time-delay fuses have relatively lower breaking currents, while quick-acting fuses require higher breaking currents. These are the fundamental characteristics of different fuse types.

说话人1: 00:41:43 - 00:42:09

These belong to high-voltage fuses, which are relatively compact in size. This section might contain products for lower voltage ranges. In low-voltage circuits, circuit breakers are more commonly used, while fuses are relatively less frequently employed. Below is an introduction regarding fuse selection.

说话人1: 00:42:09 - 00:43:28

The selection principles for fuses and circuit breakers are similar, but differences exist in motor protection applications. According to Canadian standards, circuit breakers must be set at 250%, whereas fuses are set at 225%. Slight variations may occur in US standards, requiring consultation with specific regulations.

The distinction between time-delay and instantaneous protection lies in: Time-delay protection requires lower current values due to energy accumulation considerations. In motor protection, long-time delay settings use lower fuse ratings, while short-time delays employ higher values. This principle equally applies to programmable controllers and variable frequency drives (VFDs).

For selective coordination, circuit breakers generally offer superior advantages with more flexible operation. We will subsequently discuss isolation switch-related content.

说话人1: 00:43:29 - 00:44:47

An isolating switch is primarily used for maintenance and manual current interruption. It is not a control device and does not provide short-circuit current protection. Its frame size ranges from 30A to 800A, with no intermediate specifications available. For instance, to interrupt a 50A current, a 60A isolating switch must be selected.

Isolating switches are categorized into general use and heavy duty types, with the latter suitable for frequent switching operations. Models equipped with fuses are called fusible disconnect switches, which can provide short-circuit current protection, while those without fuses are non-fusible.

Isolating switches are typically housed in enclosures with protection ratings compliant with NEMA/CSA standards, such as NEMA1 or NEMA4.
